# dsh-reprise
**An exploration loop whose conclusions you can check.**

> A DeepSeek Harness bundle: reproduce a published number, then iterate on the reproduction under
>
control — deterministic phases, a baseline the run measures itself and then freezes, a spend ledger

> that reserves before it spends, and a stop decision computed from recorded facts rather than
> rem

before it spends, and a stop decision computed from recorded facts rather than
> remembered intent.
### What it adds
| Surface | Identifier | What it does |
| Model tool | `reprise_status` | the run's progress as JSON, read-only, from the same projection th

e page draws |
| Sidebar panel | `sidebar.panellist` id `reprise`, order `25`, plus `main` key `repr
ise` | the **Reprise** button (one name in both languages — the product name is not translated) and

the page it opens; labels follow the active language (`en`, `zh`) |
| HTTP routes | `GET /api/repris
e/{overview,rounds,candidate,tree,conclusion,calls,call}` | the four views, the search tree and the

model-call audit, each read through its own read-only handle |
| Static assets | `GET /api/reprise/p
age`, `/api/reprise/dashboard.js`, `/api/reprise/format.js` | a standalone page for a host with no c

lient slots, with the formatting module the page and the panel share |
| CLI | `node packages/core/l
ib/cli/run.js --workspace <dir> --config <file>` | the same wiring the host ticks, driven by a loop;

exit 0 conclusion, 1 no comparable metric, 2 usage, 3 timeout |
| CLI | `node packages/core/lib/cli
/dump.js --candidate <id>` | timeline, every gate verdict, the gate chain step by step, the candidat
e's worktree path and whether it is still on disk, identity bindings, frontier position, and why the

run stopped |
| CLI | `node packages/core/lib/cli/dump.js --overview` | the workspace page: cards a

nd queue, the best result, and the measured/published comparison |
| CLI | `node packages/core/lib/c
li/dump.js --tree` | the search as a lineage: who branched from whom, and the reason each branch end

s |
| CLI | `node packages/core/lib/cli/dump.js --calls` / `--call <ref>` | the model-call audit, an

d one call with its prompt and response verbatim |
| CLI | `node packages/core/lib/cli/intents.js pl
ace <kind>` / `list` | human intents (`proposal`, `grant`, `anchor`, `pause`, `resume`, `approval`,

`experience`) written into `<workspace>/pending/` |
| CLI | `node packages/core/lib/cli/jobs.js list
` / `reap --job <id>` | the cluster job ledger: our jobs as the cluster lists them, the orphans (our

marker, no ledger row), and the only way an orphan is ever stopped |
[该节后续省略]
### Step 5 — ask why
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Timeline, every gate conclusion, the identity bindings, the frontier position, and why the run stopp

ed —
from the fact plane alone. `r1-h2` is the winner the shipped example produces; use whatever ste

p 4
printed. No `--config` is needed: the run records the metric contract and the stop rules into th

e
workspace at INIT, so a reader with only the directory gets the same answer. Add `--rebuild` to re

play
the whole event stream and check the materialised view still follows from the facts.
What the example does not exercise: a live model (`recorded/judgement.json` replays four answers) an

d a
real coding harness (`apply-change.mjs` applies the hypothesis mechanically). Both are configura

tion —
`model.command` and `candidate.command`. `examples/feed-structure/README.md`
says what to cha
nge and what stays unverified.
#### What the model sees
Two ways, both read-only and neither on a critical path.
`reprise_status` is the only tool the bundle registers. Its input is `candidate` (an optional id, fo

r
that candidate's page instead of the overview) and `events` (0–20, default 6). It answers with the
envelope the HTTP routes serve — `view`, `workspace`, `cursor`, `data`, an `incremental.events` lis

t —
trimmed to six facts and ten frontier members; when a workspace has no facts yet it says so with
`data: null` and a reason instead of failing. Refusals carry `ok: false` and a `reason`. The whole

fact
stream is never a tool result.
Inside the loop, the model is a subprocess: at each of the five call sites it reads one `SKILL.md` f

rom
the domain pack plus JSON facts (candidate identity, L1 check results, the metrics the monitor r

eported), and
answers in a wire format the judge parses. It is never handed the fact plane, a sessio

n, or another
candidate's outcome.
## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
These limits define when this is a poor fit — they are not a task list.

- **Verified offline only.** The phase machine, validators, identity chain, fact plane, ledger,
fron

tier, stop rules, executor and harness ports, `dump`, and the five-command path all run in
`npm test

`. Not verified end to end here: a live model, a real coding harness, a real cluster, and a
browser

actually loading the page against a real host.
- **Not on npm.** Every package is `private`, version

ed `0.0.0`, and depends on its siblings through
`workspace:*`. What installs is the release tarball

`scripts/build-release.mjs` packs — not a
registry package, and not the git URL.
- **The shipped bun

dle patch carries no config, on purpose.** The package cannot know where your
workspace is, so it sh

ips the row and nothing else; a `reprise-core` entry in your profile patch
supplies everything, and

`cordis.example.yml` beside the patch is a filled-in worked example. A
run with no config is one log

line, not a mount.
- **No host-side config schema.** The package exports no `Config`, so the Plugin

Manager cannot render
or validate the row; `config.js` is the only validator, and its verdict is a

log line.
- **No write surface.** Pause, resume, grant and approvals arrive as files under `<workspa

ce>/pending/`
(`intents.js`), not as HTTP calls.
- **One workspace, one run.** Two runs in one direc

tory are not a supported configuration; two
workspaces are two independent dashboards.
- **`packages

/exec-python` is a manifest.** No code, no `torch` import; the proxy-metric bridge is
deferred.
